security_threats.asset: editor buffer, route isolation, and local endpoint identity
controls: private OS-local endpoint with restrictive user/session access
32-byte random session capability compared in constant time
peer process/session or effective-uid verification
exact route and endpoint-instance binding
strictly increasing buffer generations with zero replay window
exact endpoint teardown and capability rotation
hostile_mutations: wrong uid, process session, route, capability, or endpoint instance
security_threats.residual_risk: A process already controlling the same user and logon session may observe or alter that user's shell; the bridge is not a sandbox against a fully compromised account.

security_threats.asset: command buffer, current directory, selection, and shell history
controls: memory-only request payload dropped immediately after response
history and frequency are separate opt-ins
history candidates come from the active shell API and never history files
metadata allowlists exclude payloads from logs, telemetry, crash reports, diagnostics, clipboard, extensions, and support bundles
secret and private provider fields never become candidates
security_threats.residual_risk: The opted-in active shell already owns its in-memory history and buffer; a compromised shell integration retains that user's shell authority.

security_threats.asset: native editor buffer, selection, cursor, and replacement span
controls: bind prompt and buffer generations, cursor byte and grapheme, selection, quoting, token context, and exact span
require UTF-8 and grapheme boundaries within the bounded buffer
retain one latest generation per pane and cancel obsolete work
native editor revalidates route, generations, buffer, cursor, selection, quoting, and span
replace exactly once without Enter
security_threats.residual_risk: A third-party native completer may return surprising text; the native editor still shows and inserts it without execution.

security_threats.asset: visible candidate identity, insertion truth, source, freshness, and risk
controls: treat labels as bounded untrusted plain text
reject or visibly contain control and unsafe format characters
separate display, insertion, source, freshness, kind, and textual risk
preserve full accessible insertion value through grapheme-safe truncation
shell returns the escaped insertion and quoting mode used
security_threats.residual_risk: Plain text may contain confusable Unicode; source, insertion disclosure, and textual risk reduce ambiguity.

security_threats.asset: native key bindings, focus, cursor, IME, pane isolation, and modal hierarchy
controls: preserve native Tab and editor bindings by default
make explicit request shortcut collision-checked, configurable, or unbound
clip popup to one pane above content and below modals
avoid cursor, IME, tabs, footer, dialogs, and sibling panes
dismiss on focus, buffer, generation, pane, prompt, modal, IME, or route invalidation
Enter dismisses and forwards native submit but never accepts
hostile_mutations: stale popup after focus loss or IME start
verification_owner: pane geometry and z-order property tests
native focus, IME, and modal automation
security_threats.residual_risk: OS IME and assistive-technology overlays vary; controlled native validation remains mandatory before release.

security_threats.asset: input latency, CPU, memory, sockets, tasks, handles, and provider isolation
controls: one latest queued generation per pane and bounded active routes
fixed buffer, frame, candidate, batch, row, cache, and deadline ceilings
application-owned joined worker stays off input, renderer, PTY, resize, and startup hot paths
no network, authentication, credential access, recursive IO, provider process, plugin process, or per-keystroke process
cancel late work and reject stale publication
join workers, close clients, remove endpoints, clear caches, and rotate capabilities on shutdown
hostile_mutations: provider or plugin invocation while typing
security_threats.residual_risk: Slow machines may miss targets; deadlines, stale-marked last-known-good state, and the immediate kill switch preserve native editing.
